Explicit analytic prerequisite restatement:
E has the same finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel/full-space structure, including dimension zero. W is C1 and exp(-W) is genuinely integrable for volume. The law mu is exactly volume.tilted(-W), whose probability normalization is derived.
D is the same closable partial gradient with exact compact smooth representative graph. epsilon is positive and forcing f is a genuine scalar L2(mu) class. No weak solution, H1 membership of a test, differentiability of u, coercivity or Poincare certificate is supplied.
All quantifiers/representatives/measures are retained: the weak equation tests every original closure-domain element; ordinary weak derivatives use volume and every C1 compact scalar test/direction; the weighted equation now uses every C1 compact scalar test, with all three products L1 for volume.
For C1 W and genuine integrability of exp(-W) volume, let mu=volume.tilted(-W). For every same closable exact compact smooth gradient D, epsilon>0 and scalar L2(mu) input f, construct u in D.closure.domain satisfying the variational equation for every domain test. Its actual closed gradient is the ordinary weak gradient, with locally volume-integrable representatives and full C1 compact directional identities. For every C1 compact psi, all three weighted volume products are integrable and epsilon integral exp(-W)u psi + integral exp(-W)<D.closure u,gradient psi> = integral exp(-W)f psi.
Same actual compact-gradient graph closure admits C1 compact function/gradient pairs; actual positive-epsilon weak resolvent has all C1 compact weighted volume tests and genuine ordinary weak gradient. Actual PBPS reflected conditional R/S law and original fixed D precede epsilon/input. No local H2, global operator-core/Bochner, conditional Poincare/BL, centered epsilon limit, noncompact constant/linear domains, measurable y-selection, SPHMC Hessian lower/full4.1, PBPS hypocoercivity or either complete main/composition. TV never transfers unbounded expected cost.

{E : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (W : E → ℝ) (hW : ContDiff ℝ 1 W)
    (hI : Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x))) :
    let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -W x)
    ∀ (D : Lp ℝ 2 μ →ₗ.[ℝ] Lp E 2 μ), D.IsClosable →
      (∀ (a : Lp ℝ 2 μ) (H : Lp E 2 μ), (a,H) ∈ D.graph ↔
        ∃ φ : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ ∧ HasCompactSupport φ ∧
          a =ᵐ[μ] φ ∧ H =ᵐ[μ] gradient φ) →
      ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∀ f : Lp ℝ 2 μ,
      ∃ u : D.closure.domain,
        (∀ v : D.closure.domain,
          ε * ⟪(u : Lp ℝ 2 μ), (v : Lp ℝ 2 μ)⟫ +
            ⟪D.closure u, D.closure v⟫ = ⟪f, (v : Lp ℝ 2 μ)⟫) ∧
        LocallyIntegrable (fun x => (u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) x) ∧
        LocallyIntegrable (fun x => D.closure u x) ∧
        (∀ ψ : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → ∀ v : E,
          Integrable (fun x => ψ x * inner ℝ (D.closure u x) v) ∧
          Integrable (fun x => (u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) x * fderiv ℝ ψ x v) ∧
          (∫ x, ψ x * inner ℝ (D.closure u x) v) =
            - ∫ x, (u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) x * fderiv ℝ ψ x v) ∧
        ∀ ψ : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ →
          Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * ((u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) x * ψ x)) ∧
          Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * inner ℝ (D.closure u x) (gradient ψ x)) ∧
          Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * (f x * ψ x)) ∧
          ε * (∫ x, Real.exp (-W x) * ((u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) x * ψ x)) +
            (∫ x, Real.exp (-W x) * inner ℝ (D.closure u x) (gradient ψ x)) =
            ∫ x, Real.exp (-W x) * (f x * ψ x)
decoder_context: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable space and canonical Lebesgue volume, including dimension zero. All section ambient instances remain part of the contract. NNReal denotes nonnegative real scalars.

Lp F 2 mu is the actual L2 quotient space; MemLp means a measurable representative with finite L2 norm. MemLp.toLp embeds the actual function class and agrees mu-a.e. Inner products of L2 classes integrate pointwise real inner products against mu.

ContDiff R 1 means C1; infinity means smooth. gradient f is the Riesz representative of the actual Frechet derivative fderiv R f. HasCompactSupport means the topological closure of nonzero support is compact.

LinearPMap is a real-linear partial operator on its stated submodule domain. Its graph consists of pairs of a domain element and its actual output. D.IsClosable means its topological graph closure is single-valued; D.closure is that same closed operator. Coercions from its domain and from L2 classes choose the usual representatives. No test membership is built into these definitions.

Measure.tilted f is exp(f)/integral exp(f) times the original measure. Probability/nonzero normalization is not built into this definition. Kernel is a measurable probability-transition family when IsMarkovKernel holds. A conditional kernel disintegrates the specified joint measure; measure.map is actual pushforward and prod is the actual independent product. stdGaussian denotes the standard real Hilbert Gaussian. All volume or law integrals specify their actual measure.

/-!
# Actual C1 compact weak-resolvent tests

The same actual closed-gradient positive-epsilon solution now permits C1 compact weighted tests. Genuine domain membership and all three weighted products are proved. Inverseweight tests remain compact; no C-infinity potential, H2/core/global Bochner/Poincare/BL certificate is assumed. PBPS Appendix C.1 and SPHMC4.1 analytic prerequisite, not a complete source theorem.
-/
set_option autoImplicit false
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.WeightedResolventC1
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory InnerProductSpace
open scoped ContDiff NNReal RealInnerProductSpace Topology
noncomputable section

theorem weak_resolvent_c1 {E : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (W : E → ℝ) (hW : ContDiff ℝ 1 W)
    (hI : Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x))) :
    let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -W x)
    ∀ (D : Lp ℝ 2 μ →ₗ.[ℝ] Lp E 2 μ), D.IsClosable →
      (∀ (a : Lp ℝ 2 μ) (H : Lp E 2 μ), (a,H) ∈ D.graph ↔
        ∃ φ : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ ∧ HasCompactSupport φ ∧
          a =ᵐ[μ] φ ∧ H =ᵐ[μ] gradient φ) →
      ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∀ f : Lp ℝ 2 μ,
      ∃ u : D.closure.domain,
        (∀ v : D.closure.domain,
          ε * ⟪(u : Lp ℝ 2 μ), (v : Lp ℝ 2 μ)⟫ +
            ⟪D.closure u, D.closure v⟫ = ⟪f, (v : Lp ℝ 2 μ)⟫) ∧
        LocallyIntegrable (fun x => (u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) x) ∧
        LocallyIntegrable (fun x => D.closure u x) ∧
        (∀ ψ : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → ∀ v : E,
          Integrable (fun x => ψ x * inner ℝ (D.closure u x) v) ∧
          Integrable (fun x => (u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) x * fderiv ℝ ψ x v) ∧
          (∫ x, ψ x * inner ℝ (D.closure u x) v) =
            - ∫ x, (u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) x * fderiv ℝ ψ x v) ∧
        ∀ ψ : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ →
          Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * ((u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) x * ψ x)) ∧
          Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * inner ℝ (D.closure u x) (gradient ψ x)) ∧
          Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * (f x * ψ x)) ∧
          ε * (∫ x, Real.exp (-W x) * ((u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) x * ψ x)) +
            (∫ x, Real.exp (-W x) * inner ℝ (D.closure u x) (gradient ψ x)) =
            ∫ x, Real.exp (-W x) * (f x * ψ x) := by
  let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -W x)
  dsimp only
  intro D hD hgraph ε hε f
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := isProbabilityMeasure_tilted hI
  obtain ⟨u,hu,_⟩ := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.ClosedGraphResolvent.weak_resolvent D.closure hD.closure_isClosed ε hε f
  obtain ⟨huL,hGL,hderiv⟩ := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.WeightedGradientDistribution.closed_gradient_distributional
    W hW hI D hD hgraph u (D.closure u) (D.closure.mem_graph u)
  refine ⟨u,hu,huL,hGL,hderiv,?_⟩
  intro ψ hψ hc
  obtain ⟨hp,hg,hpqc⟩ := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.CompactC1GradientDomain.compact_c1_in_closed_gradient μ D hD hgraph hψ hc
  let p : Lp ℝ 2 μ := hp.toLp ψ
  let q : Lp E 2 μ := hg.toLp (gradient ψ)
  obtain ⟨v,hv,hDv⟩ := D.closure.mem_graph_iff.mp hpqc
  have he := hu v
  rw [hv,hDv] at he
  have hpe (a : Lp ℝ 2 μ) :
      (fun x => inner ℝ (a x) (p x)) =ᵐ[μ] (fun x => a x * ψ x) := by
    filter_upwards [hp.coeFn_toLp] with x hx
    rw [show p x = ψ x from hx]
    simp [mul_comm]
  have hge :
      (fun x => inner ℝ (D.closure u x) (q x)) =ᵐ[μ]
        (fun x => inner ℝ (D.closure u x) (gradient ψ x)) := by
    filter_upwards [hg.coeFn_toLp] with x hx
    rw [show q x = gradient ψ x from hx]
  have hiu := (L2.integrable_inner (𝕜 := ℝ) (u : Lp ℝ 2 μ) p).congr (hpe u)
  have hiG := (L2.integrable_inner (𝕜 := ℝ) (D.closure u) q).congr hge
  have hif := (L2.integrable_inner (𝕜 := ℝ) f p).congr (hpe f)
  have hwu := (integrable_tilted_iff hI _).mp hiu
  have hwG := (integrable_tilted_iff hI _).mp hiG
  have hwf := (integrable_tilted_iff hI _).mp hif
  simp only [smul_eq_mul] at hwu hwG hwf
  refine ⟨hwu,hwG,hwf,?_⟩
  rw [L2.inner_def, L2.inner_def, L2.inner_def,
    integral_congr_ae (hpe u), integral_congr_ae hge,
    integral_congr_ae (hpe f)] at he
  have ht (g : E → ℝ) : (∫ x, g x ∂μ) =
      (∫ x, Real.exp (-W x))⁻¹ * ∫ x, Real.exp (-W x) * g x := by
    rw [show μ = (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -W x) from rfl, integral_tilted]
    rw [← integral_const_mul]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upwards [] with x
    change (Real.exp (-W x) / (∫ z, Real.exp (-W z))) • g x = _
    simp only [smul_eq_mul, div_eq_mul_inv]
    ring
  rw [ht,ht,ht] at he
  apply mul_left_cancel₀ (inv_ne_zero (integral_exp_pos hI).ne')
  convert he using 1
  ring

end
end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.WeightedResolventC1

reconstruction.text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure,including dimension zero. Let W:E->R be globally C1 and suppose exp(-W) is Bochner integrable against canonical Lebesgue volume. Define the actual measure
  mu=volume.tilted(x -> -W(x)),
meaning normalized density exp(-W)/integral exp(-W)dvolume relative to volume. The tilt definition alone does not include a probability or nonzero-normalization certificate.
For every real linear partial operator D:L2(mu;R)->L2(mu;E),assume D is closable and that,for all scalar a and vector H L2 classes,
  (a,H) in graph(D) if and only if there exists smooth compactly supported phi:E->R
  with a=phi mu-almost everywhere and H=grad phi mu-almost everywhere.
Then for every real epsilon>0 and every input f in L2(mu;R),there exists u in the domain of T=closure(D) with all of the following properties. Write ubar,fbar for the usual representatives of the scalar classes u,f,and G for the representative of the actual vector class T u.
  (a) For every v in domain(T),with its scalar class and actual vector output T v,
        epsilon <u,v>_{L2(mu;R)}+<T u,T v>_{L2(mu;E)}
          =<f,v>_{L2(mu;R)}.
  (b) ubar:E->R is locally Bochner integrable with respect to volume.
  (c) G:E->E is locally Bochner integrable with respect to volume.
  (d) For every globally C1 compactly supported real psi:E->R and every direction e in E,
        psi(x)<G(x),e> and ubar(x)D psi(x)[e]
      are both integrable against volume,and
        integral psi(x)<G(x),e> dvolume(x)
          =-integral ubar(x)D psi(x)[e] dvolume(x).
  (e) For every globally C1 compactly supported real psi,the following three real integrands are integrable against volume:
        exp(-W(x))(ubar(x)psi(x)),
        exp(-W(x))<G(x),grad psi(x)>,
        exp(-W(x))(fbar(x)psi(x)),
      and the exact weighted test identity holds:
        epsilon integral exp(-W)(ubar psi)dvolume
          +integral exp(-W)<G,grad psi>dvolume
          =integral exp(-W)(fbar psi)dvolume.
The Frechet derivative and gradient of the test functions are actual derivatives. Domain and L2-class coercions use their usual representatives. The unannotated local integrability,Integrable assertions and integrals are with respect to canonical Lebesgue volume;the Hilbert inner products in (a) are instead under the actual mu. The last identity uses the unnormalized weight exp(-W),not an inserted density-normalization factor.
The solution u is fixed before every variational or compact-test quantifier;the same actual T u is used throughout. No uniqueness claim,solution norm bound,mean-zero restriction on f,additional C2 hypothesis on W,dense-domain premise for the supplied D,or existence of D is asserted. Probability normalization of mu is not an extra stated conjunct.
